opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesus Cooke (employee ID E029) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E029.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jesus Cooke (E029) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max allowed is write (admin only for role owners; Source Code is owned by Engineer). Requested level equals max, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jesus Cooke (E029) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors with basic training max out at read for Source Code (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on Jesus Cooke's employment status. HR lists him as full-time (max write for Source Code), while Security DB lists him as a contractor with basic security training. For contractors with basic training, the maximum allowed for Source Code is read (write requires advanced training; admin is never allowed for contractors). Because the requested write level exceeds the maximum under the contractor classification, I grant the maximum allowed: read. I chose the more conservative classification given the conflicting evidence to avoid over-granting access.
